summary: The built-in Cinatra assistant's ONE tag is @cinatra (cinatra#1880, Epic #1873 W5 — owner ruling 2026-07-23 (groganz)). Operator-upgrade twin of the fresh-install bootstrap change in src/lib/assistant-registry-schema.ts, which STOPPED seeding the cinatra -> @cinatra-ai/cinatra-assistant builtin alias. WHY: the built-in's resolving tag is its HANDLE; the old builtin alias occupied the cinatra token in the shared handle+alias namespace, so the boot handle mint (registerAssistantHandle: base, base-2, ... across BOTH tables) suffixed the built-in handle to cinatra-2 and the surface showed @cinatra-2. This migration converges an already-deployed database to the fresh-install shape: (1) DELETE the legacy builtin alias row (cinatra, source='builtin', package @cinatra-ai/cinatra-assistant) to free the token, scoped to the builtin source + reserved package so a manifest/admin alias on the same token is untouched; (2) RENAME the built-in principal's resolving handle to cinatra, identifying the principal by its reserved Better-Auth username ('cinatra', userType 'assistant'), guarded + idempotent (only when the current handle is not already cinatra AND no other principal's handle holds cinatra — defensive against the assistant_handles.handle UNIQUE). End state (fresh AND upgraded): handle cinatra, no builtin alias — one tag, @cinatra; chat routing resolves @cinatra to the built-in through the handle registry (resolveAssistantHandles), unchanged. SEQ: strictly greater than the max shipped/open seq (core__0075 widget-auth-token-keys-canonical max on origin/main; core__0076 assistant-pause rides the same #1880 lane; no open PR ships a higher core__ seq), so this slice is core__0077. IDEMPOTENT: a second run is a no-op (alias already gone; handle already cinatra so the guarded UPDATE matches nothing); on a fresh-bootstrap DB the seed was never written and the handle was minted as cinatra, so the ledger-faked migration would also be a no-op. Single per-migration transaction; unqualified names resolve to the app schema on the runner's search_path, public."user" is the Better-Auth principal table (same database). down() is a best-effort inverse: rename the handle back to cinatra-2 (when free) and re-insert the builtin alias, restoring a valid pre-fix state. migrations/** is HIGH-RISK: owner approval required; the lane never merges. destructive=true (an alias row is removed and a handle value is rewritten — user-land data affected).
